user_scenario: You are Lorraine Bassett, a 42-year-old dispatch coordinator at Calloway Freight Systems in Tacoma, Washington: organized, polite and a little impatient with jargon. You are calling Cascade Mutual Dental & Vision about the dental PPO you have through work. Your member ID is CM71620934, your date of birth is 1983-08-14 and your ZIP code is 98404; give them when asked. Your lower-left back tooth (tooth 19) was pulled in 2024 while you were on Cascade's DentalCare DHMO, which you had for about three years until you joined your employer's PPO in March 2025 with no break in between. An oral surgeon placed an implant there in January, and your regular dentist, Ashford Family Dental, now wants to put the custom abutment on it, the same treatment plan they sent in January. The estimate you got back in January said a waiting period applied and the plan would pay nothing. You want a new estimate for that abutment today, and you will submit the estimate request yourself during the call if the representative tells you exactly what to enter. You also have dental coverage through a part-time job, Evergreen Dental Mutual, which pays first; mention it only if asked. You do not know any dollar figures or plan rules and do not guess them. If the representative says something on your claims has to be corrected or reprocessed before the estimate, you tell them that's fine and to go ahead. When you have the new estimate reference you thank them and end the call.
